Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. Don't ask ChatGPT, "What digital product should I sell?" Instead, ask: "What problems are people currently paying to solve?" Then, pick one problem you genuinely understand. One of the biggest mistakes new digital sellers make is starting with the product. They ask: "What e-book should I make?" or "What template should I sell?" This is backwards. Start with the problem. People don't buy a PDF because they desperately want another file on their phone. They buy because they want to: 1. Save money 2. Save time 3. Learn something faster 4. Get organized 5. Avoid mistakes 6. Reach a specific goal So, open ChatGPT and ask: "What problems are people currently paying to solve? Give me 20 problems that could be turned into simple digital products. For each one, tell me who has the problem, what result they want, and what type of digital product could help?" Don't create anything yet! Just look at the 20 problems first. Tomorrow, I'll show you what to do with this list. Save this prompt and follow for Part Two. #ChatGPTprompts #digitalproducts #facelessbusiness #digitalproductideas #onlinebusiness
